solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unimportant item gazed upon, sin recalled in it

indicators.note: the reversed pair is placed inside the two letters of the word it
called back, so the pair of words is read from end to start

parts.note: navel-gazing is self-absorbed contemplation, so the navel is the thing stared at
to err is to sin or go wrong

explanation.surface: A trivial object being stared at while some wrongdoing is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NAVEL + ERR into RRELEVAN, which goes 'in' IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beside the point is of no consequence, a direct synonym for unimportant.

clue.text: In the soup, my dear, nine of the ingredients pre-blended

indicators.note: in the soup is slang for in trouble or in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cook telling a loved one that most of the soup's ingredients came pre-mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' scrambles MY DEAR into READYM.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready-mix is a commercial blend, such as cement or cake mix, with the dry components already combined.

clue.text: Spirit soared briefly upward

indicators.note: in a down clue, upward means the letters are read from bottom to top
cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: flew is a synonym of soared

explanation.surface: A ghost or soul rising quickly into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts FLEW to FLE; 'upward' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a sprite, a small supernatural being, which is one kind of spirit.

clue.text: Once having worry, leave

parts.note: ex means former, as once does
something eating you is worrying you, so eat means to worry

explanation.surface: Someone who used to be anxious finally departing.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is permission for a pupil to be away from a British boarding school, or a student from college.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is formal permission to be absent, i.e. a grant of leave.

clue.text: What can be stretched to cut some maintenance

indicators.note: the car goes into the middle of the word for some, cutting it in two

parts.note: any can mean some, as in have you any money
a stretch limo is a lengthened limousine

explanation.surface: Asking what can be stretched in order to trim the upkeep costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimony is court-ordered financial support paid to a former spouse, which British usage also calls maintenance.

clue.text: One leaning over a river ending in Liffey in Irish county

parts.note: one who tips, leaning something over, is a tipper

indicators.note: only the final letter of the river's name is taken

explanation.surface: Someone bending over a river in Ireland at the end of the Liffey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liffey is the river through Dublin; it is there only to supply its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is one of the thirty-two counties of Ireland, in the province of Munster.

clue.text: Zero European capital lacking in Russian city

parts.note: O looks like the figure nought

indicators.note: the capital's name is missing the word in

parts.note: Minsk is the capital of Belarus

explanation.surface: A Russian city with nothing of a European capital in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in south-western Siberia, Russia, on the Irtysh river.

clue.text: Past one's peak then?

parts.note: a climber who has gone beyond the summit is literally on the far side of the rise

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being too old for something is read literally as a walker gone beyond the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means past one's prime, especially through age.

clue.text: God put wind beneath it

indicators.note: in a down clue, the twisting word sits below the word for it

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for it
to wind is to turn, as a key

explanation.surface: A deity setting a breeze underneath something.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the Roman god of agriculture and time, father of Jupiter.

clue.text: One having fled prison, Alcatraz finally consumed by raging fire that's hot!

indicators.note: the letter for one has escaped and is gone from the word

parts.note: a jail is a prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed up inside the jumbled flames
a raging fire is out of control, so its letters are scrambled
only the last letter of the prison island is used

explanation.surface: An inmate escapes Alcatraz as a furious blaze takes hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raging' is the anagram signal on the blaze word, and 'consumed by' puts the prison's last letter among those letters. A jalfrezi is a curry, so 'hot' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalfrezi is a spicy curry with chillies, so on a menu it is a fiery, hot choice.

clue.text: Quite fair

definitions.meaning: the adverb as in rather good, moderately
the adjective as in good-looking, attractive

explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means moderately; as an adjective it means attractive, as fair does in old usage.

clue.text: Small bird or seal you might catch

indicators.note: catching a word means hearing it, so this is how it is heard

parts.note: a signet is a seal, as on a signet ring

explanation.surface: A little bird, or a seal you could capture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' looks like trapping the animal; here it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, so a small one of the bird kind.

clue.text: Nothing in books covered by practice of American space exploration?

indicators.note: the agency's practice, its usage, follows its name
the books sit inside the agency's name, which covers them

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
usage is customary practice

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is nothing in the books about NASA's way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is British slang meaning nothing at all, as in we got not a sausage.

clue.text: Capsize in open vessel

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat tipping over when it is an open-decked craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to tip over, synonymous with the verb overturn.

clue.text: Extremely tasty, a rich baked confection — such as this?

definitions.text: Extremely tasty, a rich baked confection — such as this?

indicators.note: a confection is a thing put together, so the letters are made into something new
only the outer letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: Describing a delicious rich cake and asking if this is one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'tasty' (TY) plus A RICH BAKED are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday cake is a rich baked confection, the very kind the clue describes.

clue.text: Bird part assimilating small fish

parts.note: a dove is a bird

indicators.note: taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A bird part of whose body absorbs a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a European flatfish prized for eating, so a fish.

clue.text: Food: time to eat Eastern dish

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: the short word for time takes in, eats, the letter

parts.note: MIN is short for minute, a unit of time

explanation.surface: Mealtime: time to eat an Asian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of stir-fried noodles, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Looker securing opening in faculty for the record confined to history?

indicators.note: the inner pieces are placed inside the word for a sense

parts.note: sight is one of the faculties or senses

indicators.note: holding on to, so the opening is enclosed

parts.note: the eye is the organ that looks
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: An observer gaining a place in a university faculty, a feat for history books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' and 'in' are both container signals, one nested in the other; 'faculty' means a sense, not a university department.
explanation.definitionFit: A seventy-eight is the old 78rpm shellac gramophone disc, now obsolete.

clue.text: A round lump primarily rough — like this?

definitions.text: A round lump primarily rough — like this?

indicators.note: rough here means roughly put together, so the letters are jumbled
only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A rounded lump, mostly rough, perhaps described this way.
explanation.walkthrough: A ROUND plus L of 'lump' are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodular means having or forming small rounded swellings, so it describes a lumpy surface.

clue.text: Very many for example taken in by celebrity

indicators.note: held inside, so the abbreviation sits within

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, as in literary lion
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Lots of people, for instance, fooled by a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means vast in number, as in their fans are legion.

clue.text: Cherry-bound paper needed

indicators.note: the paper is tied in, bound, by the colour word

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red
a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: A paper needed that is bound in cherry red.
explanation.definitionFit: Required is a synonym of needed, both meaning necessary.

clue.text: Country straddling a wide lake

indicators.note: the country's name stands with legs either side of the inner letters

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
W abbreviates wide, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A nation that sits across a broad lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' wants to be the definition, but it is only MALI; the answer is defined by 'lake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Malawi is one of the great African Rift Valley lakes, as well as the name of a country.

clue.text: Coffee, second brew

parts.note: mo is a moment, as in wait a mo
cha is slang for tea, a brew

explanation.surface: Coffee, as a second hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee named after the Yemeni port, or coffee flavoured with chocolate.

clue.text: Famous Sevillian fruit, orange, not half round!

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

indicators.note: turned round, the kept letters run backwards
only half of the colour word is kept, its first three letters

explanation.surface: A Seville fruit, the orange, not even half round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first half of the colour word, and 'round' turns it backwards. Seville oranges set the false scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the barber of Seville in the plays of Beaumarchais and the operas of Rossini and Mozart.

clue.text: Don Corleone initially in film hampered by siren?

indicators.note: held back within, so the inner piece is surrounded

parts.note: a siren is one who lures, a lurer

indicators.note: the initial goes inside the film title

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film

indicators.note: only the first letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: Mafia boss Don Corleone in a movie, held back by a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'hampered by' are nested container signals. Don Corleone of The Godfather is a decoy: a don is a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge, so a lecturer.

clue.text: Some drug habit — yuk!

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Disgust at someone's drug habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugh and yuk are both interjections expressing disgust.

clue.text: Bet poet needs no introduction

indicators.note: the poet's first letter is removed

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A famous wager-making poet who is too well-known to introduce.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put up in poker before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Graduate in his anger unfortunately gives severe scolding

indicators.note: the degree goes inside the jumbled letters
things going badly signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate's angry outburst amounts to a severe telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles HIS ANGER into EARSHING, with BA set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a long harangue or telling-off, a scolding at length.
